Create an add-factor

addf.Rd

An add-factor is a series added to a forecast to shift it for a while. addf() returns one that is zero over the bank except where you set it: along a straight-line ramp, along several ramps that add up, or through points given as formulas.

Usage

addf(
  start = bank_start(),
  end = bank_end(),
  from = 0,
  to = 0,
  ser_name = "value",
  per = "year",
  ...,
  interp = c("linear", "stine")
)

Arguments

start

date the ramp starts, in any form to_ymd() reads ("2026Q3", 2026.3, "2026M07", 2026), or a data frame of ramps with columns start, end, from and to, one ramp per row. A day ("2026-07-01") must be the first day of a period at frequency per.

end

date the ramp ends

from

value at start

to

value at end

ser_name

name of the series

per

frequency: "year" (default), "quarter" or "month". A start written as a quarter ("2026Q3", 2026.3) or a month ("2026M07") sets it.

...

with formulas: further points (see details)

interp

with formulas: how to join the points, "linear" (default) or "stine", the Stineman spline, which eases in and out of each point without overshooting. Must be named.

Value

one xts series over the bank, from getOption("fcutils.bnk_start") to getOption("fcutils.bnk_end") (see make_xts()). A ramp that starts before the bank or ends after it extends the series past the bank.

Details

A ramp runs in equal steps from from at start to to at end. Before start and after end the add-factor is zero, so a ramp that ends away from zero drops back to zero in the next period. With no arguments, addf() gives zeros over the bank.

Given a data frame of ramps, addf() builds one add-factor per row and returns their sum, so overlapping ramps add up. A data frame with no rows gives zeros over the bank, at the frequency per. A date column must be all numbers or all strings.

Given formulas, addf(2026.3 ~ 0, 2027.4 ~ -0.3, 2030.4 ~ 0), the add-factor runs through the points in straight lines, one equal step per period, and is zero before the first point and after the last. Each formula has a date on the left and a value on the right, and each date must start a period within the bank. Give at least two points. The frequency follows the date of the first formula (2026.3 is a quarter), unless per is given by name; ser_name and per must be named. Decimal dates are quarters, so monthly points need strings ("2026M10" ~ 1).

With interp = "stine" the points are joined by a smooth curve instead. The spline treats the zeros before the first point and after the last as known, so an add-factor that starts and ends at zero leaves and returns to zero gradually. A ramp joins only two points, so interp applies to formulas, not to start, end, from and to or a table of ramps.

Examples

options(
  fcutils.bnk_start = as.Date("2020-01-01"),
  fcutils.bnk_end = as.Date("2035-12-31")
)
# one ramp: from 0 in 2026Q3 to -0.3 in 2027Q4, zero outside
addf("2026Q3", "2027Q4", 0, -0.3)[p(2026.2, 2028.1)]
#>            value
#> 2026-04-01  0.00
#> 2026-07-01  0.00
#> 2026-10-01 -0.06
#> 2027-01-01 -0.12
#> 2027-04-01 -0.18
#> 2027-07-01 -0.24
#> 2027-10-01 -0.30
#> 2028-01-01  0.00
# a ramp that ends away from zero drops back to zero after its end
addf(2026.3, 2027.4, 1, 2, ser_name = "ECT_HI")[p(2027.3, 2028.2)]
#>            ECT_HI
#> 2027-07-01    1.8
#> 2027-10-01    2.0
#> 2028-01-01    0.0
#> 2028-04-01    0.0
# annual and monthly
addf(2026, 2028, 0, 1)[p(2025, 2029)]
#>            value
#> 2025-01-01   0.0
#> 2026-01-01   0.0
#> 2027-01-01   0.5
#> 2028-01-01   1.0
#> 2029-01-01   0.0
addf("2026M01", "2026M06", 0, 0.5)[p("2025M12", "2026M07")]
#>            value
#> 2025-12-01   0.0
#> 2026-01-01   0.0
#> 2026-02-01   0.1
#> 2026-03-01   0.2
#> 2026-04-01   0.3
#> 2026-05-01   0.4
#> 2026-06-01   0.5
#> 2026-07-01   0.0
# zeros over the bank
addf(per = "quarter")[p(2026.1, 2026.4)]
#>            value
#> 2026-01-01     0
#> 2026-04-01     0
#> 2026-07-01     0
#> 2026-10-01     0

# several ramps at once: down to -0.3 by 2027Q4, then back to 0 by 2030Q4
ramps <- tibble::tribble(
  ~start,   ~end,     ~from, ~to,
  "2026Q3", "2027Q4", 0,     -0.3,
  "2028Q1", "2030Q4", -0.3,  0
)
ramps_adj <- addf(ramps)
round(ramps_adj[p(2026.2, 2031.1)], 3)
#>             value
#> 2026-04-01  0.000
#> 2026-07-01  0.000
#> 2026-10-01 -0.060
#> 2027-01-01 -0.120
#> 2027-04-01 -0.180
#> 2027-07-01 -0.240
#> 2027-10-01 -0.300
#> 2028-01-01 -0.300
#> 2028-04-01 -0.273
#> 2028-07-01 -0.245
#> 2028-10-01 -0.218
#> 2029-01-01 -0.191
#> 2029-04-01 -0.164
#> 2029-07-01 -0.136
#> 2029-10-01 -0.109
#> 2030-01-01 -0.082
#> 2030-04-01 -0.055
#> 2030-07-01 -0.027
#> 2030-10-01  0.000
#> 2031-01-01  0.000
# the same as points, with decimal or quoted dates
pts_adj <- addf(2026.3 ~ 0, 2027.4 ~ -0.3, 2028.1 ~ -0.3, 2030.4 ~ 0)
all.equal(pts_adj, ramps_adj)
#> [1] TRUE
addf("2026Q3" ~ 0, "2027Q4" ~ -0.3, "2028Q1" ~ -0.3, "2030Q4" ~ 0)[p(2027.3, 2028.2)]
#>                 value
#> 2027-07-01 -0.2400000
#> 2027-10-01 -0.3000000
#> 2028-01-01 -0.3000000
#> 2028-04-01 -0.2727273
# a smooth curve through the same points
smooth_adj <- addf(2026.3 ~ 0, 2027.4 ~ -0.3, 2028.1 ~ -0.3, 2030.4 ~ 0,
                   interp = "stine")
round(tsbox::ts_c(linear = pts_adj, stine = smooth_adj)[p(2026.2, 2031.1)], 3)
#>            linear  stine
#> 2026-04-01  0.000  0.000
#> 2026-07-01  0.000  0.000
#> 2026-10-01 -0.060 -0.031
#> 2027-01-01 -0.120 -0.106
#> 2027-04-01 -0.180 -0.194
#> 2027-07-01 -0.240 -0.269
#> 2027-10-01 -0.300 -0.300
#> 2028-01-01 -0.300 -0.300
#> 2028-04-01 -0.273 -0.293
#> 2028-07-01 -0.245 -0.274
#> 2028-10-01 -0.218 -0.245
#> 2029-01-01 -0.191 -0.210
#> 2029-04-01 -0.164 -0.170
#> 2029-07-01 -0.136 -0.130
#> 2029-10-01 -0.109 -0.090
#> 2030-01-01 -0.082 -0.055
#> 2030-04-01 -0.055 -0.026
#> 2030-07-01 -0.027 -0.007
#> 2030-10-01  0.000  0.000
#> 2031-01-01  0.000  0.000
